'''Michael Russell Wheldon Rands''' (born 2 August 1956) is a British [[conservation biologist]]. He is the Master of [[Darwin College, Cambridge]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.darwin.cam.ac.uk/dr-michael-rands|title=Mike Rands at Darwin College, Cambridge|access-date=2020-10-07|archive-date=5 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205022406/https://www.darwin.cam.ac.uk/dr-michael-rands|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a fellow at the [[Cambridge Judge Business School]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/faculty-research/subject-groups/organisational-theory-information-systems/#item-2|title=Honorary appointments at Cambridge Judge Business School|access-date=2020-10-07}}</ref> He was previously the executive director of the [[Cambridge Conservation Initiative]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cambridgeconservation.org/cci-team|title=Cambridge Conservation Initiative|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref> Prior to this he was chief executive of [[BirdLife International]].

==Early life and education==
Rands was born on 2 August 1956.<ref name="WW 2020">{{cite web |title=Rands, Dr Michael Russell Wheldon, (born 2 Aug. 1956), Executive Director, Cambridge Conservation Initiative, since 2009 |website=[[Who's Who 2020]] |publisher=Oxford University Press |url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-31881 |doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U31881 |date=1 December 2019|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4 }}</ref> He was educated at [[Dartington Hall School]], the [[University of East Anglia]] and the [[University of Oxford]]. He gained his doctorate in [[ecology]] at the [[Edward Grey Institute of Field Ornithology]], Department of Zoology and [[Wolfson College, Oxford]].

==Career==
After his DPhil, Rands carried out post-doctoral research with the [[Game & Wildlife Conservation Trust]], conducting field experiments that helped establish the [[Conservation headland]] as a method for increasing wildlife populations in agricultural ecosystems, a practice that became enshrined in UK and EU legislation and policy.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://publications.naturalengland.org.uk/publication/64014|title=English Nature report on wildlife gain from agri-environment schemes 2001|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref> In 1986 he joined the International Council for Bird Preservation as programme director where he played a leading role in creating [[BirdLife International]]. He became director of strategic planning and policy at BirdLife International in 1994 before becoming its chief executive from 1996 to 2009.<ref name="WW 2020" />

In 2009 he became the founding director of the [[Cambridge Conservation Initiative]] (CCI). He led the creation of the Cambridge Conservation Campus, endorsed by [[Sir David Attenborough]], within the flagship David Attenborough Building, which opened in 2013.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cam.ac.uk/news/cambridge-conservation-campus-launched|title=Sir David Attenborough opens the Cambridge Conservation Campus in April 2013|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref> In 2018, under his leadership, CCI launched the Endangered Landscapes Programme, a collaboration with the Arcadia Fund to restore European landscapes for life.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.endangeredlandscapes.org/|title=Endangered Landscapes Programme|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=atWMReAMqsA|title=Mike Rands introduces the launch of the Endangered Landscapes Programme in October 2018|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref>

In October 2019, it was announced that he had been elected as Master of [[Darwin College, Cambridge]]: he took up the post on 1 October 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.darwin.cam.ac.uk/news/election-next-master-darwin-college|title=Election of the next Master of Darwin College|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref> He is also a Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the University of Cambridge <ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2021-22/special/01/section1.shtml|title=Deputy Vice-Chancellors appointed|access-date=2021-11-17}}</ref> and Trustee of the Cambridge Commonwealth, European & International Trust.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cambridgetrust.org/about/trustees/|title=Cambridge Trust Trustees|access-date=2020-10-07}}</ref> In 2021, the University of East Anglia announced that he would receive an Honorary Doctorate in Science in July 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.uea.ac.uk/web/about/alumni-and-supporters/graduation/honorary-graduates-2022/-/categories/5505422|title=UEA honorary graduates 2022|access-date=2021-11-17}}</ref>
